state.objective: Stress-test first-release policy for a Ruby CIBA OP gem whose user wants alignment with node-oidc-provider. The user explicitly requests reconsidering non-preferred alternatives. Prior numeric answers and assistant recommendation are intentionally withheld. Earlier scope and transaction decisions are relevant constraints but are open to explicit revision for this comparison. Compare strongest credible cases rather than rewarding the status quo or full parity automatically.
earlier_explicit_scope: Public OSS gem, first consumer is own company
CIBA protocol only; customer approval UI, upstream identity and delegation are application owned
Initial release poll and login_hint only; signed authentication requests and user_code excluded
Same Sequel DB as rodauth-oauth; transactional before/after hooks with rollback; best-effort post-commit observation
No certification or specific external CIBA client required
state.new_scope_ambiguity: The later alignment instruction does not explicitly state whether all optional node features must now ship in the first release. No named initial consumer requires ping, other hints, claims/resource/RAR or signed requests. Do not equate absence of demand with a ban on implementing them.
state.implementation: Saved consent Grant separated from requests; account/client/scope/expiry checks; result API; trigger after persistence before response; 600s default; request replay revokes related Grant/token rows; denied result consumed once; expiry checked first. Tests: 104 runs/757 assertions Ruby4.0.6 SQLite. Isolated original node handler/helper tests pass with persistence/issuance/revocation stubs. No complete node OP execution; no latest PostgreSQL/MySQL tests due Docker socket permission denial.
state.failure_facts: Gem issuance/signing/hook exception rolls back request consumption plus token DB rows in the same transaction, allowing another poll. A committed success/lost response is not replayable; replay revokes. Node handler consumes before grant validation and issuance. With the harness nontransactional memory persistence, a failure leaves consumption intact; next poll rejects and revokes. The harness does not establish behavior for every node adapter. Both designs must prevent duplicate usable tokens and retain client isolation.

options_tradeoffs.commit_consumption: Closer to observed node handler retry behavior; requires separate consumption/issuance transaction boundary and revised hook contract; failure forces a new customer approval request; DB token changes could still roll back within issuance.
options_tradeoffs.atomic_rollback: Preserves existing same-DB all-or-nothing issuance and hook contract; permits retry after rolled-back failure, but differs from observed node retry behavior and must be documented honestly.
options_tradeoffs.configurable: Could support both, but adds configuration/testing/state semantics before first release.

# 状態変更の拡張点を Rodauth の before / after 慣例に合わせる

CIBA の主要な状態変更に、Rodauth の慣例に沿う before / after フックを設ける。専用フックを設けない案や独自の拡張機構を追加する案に対し、基盤と同じカスタマイズ方法を維持することを優先する。これらは監査専用ではなく、監査機能の導入を CIBA の利用条件にしない。

before / after フックは状態変更と同じ DB トランザクション内で呼ぶ。after は commit 後ではない。フックから伝播する例外では DB の変更をロールバックするが、外部システムへの副作用までは取り消せない。具体的なフック名・対象となる状態変更・エラー応答は今後設計する。

任意の観測用イベントは別の契約とし、通知先の失敗で CIBA の成否を変えず、障害を報告する。Rodauth の既存 audit_logging と CIBA の連携可能範囲は、実装時に検証する。

根拠: [Rodauth の create_account 実装](https://github.com/jeremyevans/rodauth/blob/master/lib/rodauth/features/create_account.rb)、[audit_logging](https://rodauth.jeremyevans.net/rdoc/files/doc/audit_logging_rdoc.html)、[製品比較](../research/idm-ciba-integration.md)。

# node-oidc-provider lifecycle reference

Run `node --experimental-vm-modules test/reference/lifecycle.mjs` (verified with Node v26.5.0).

The two JavaScript fixtures are unchanged sources from the v9.12.2 release, fetched using the GitHub connector on 2026-09-30:

- [CIBA handler](https://github.com/panva/node-oidc-provider/blob/v9.12.2/lib/actions/grants/ciba.js)
- [Source helper](https://github.com/panva/node-oidc-provider/blob/v9.12.2/lib/helpers/grant_source.js)

Their MIT license is retained alongside them. These files are reference tests, not dependencies of the Ruby gem.

The harness executes both real modules using native VM modules. It substitutes deterministic in-memory persistence, token issuance and revocation, context validation, presence checks and attestation binding. It verifies the actual handler/helper ordering for pending, denial, failed issuance/replay and expired consumption. It cannot establish full OP interoperability, cryptographic behavior, adapter atomicity, or behavior of node's global HTTP error middleware.

In particular, consumed state survives a simulated issuance exception because the test persistence has no outer transaction. A deployment-specific transactional adapter may behave differently. The gem's existing transaction rollback is an observed difference, not evidence that either implementation is insecure.

gem_token_issuance.text:
def create_token(grant_type)
      return super unless grant_type == CibaSupport::GRANT_TYPE
      row = ciba_locked_row(ciba_ds.where(ciba_values(
        auth_req_id_digest: Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(param("auth_req_id")),
        oauth_application_id: oauth_application[oauth_applications_id_column])))
      ciba_error("invalid_grant") unless row
      ciba_error("expired_token") if row[:expires_at] <= ciba_now
      if row[:status] == "consumed"
        revoke_ciba_grant(row[:grant_id]) if row[:grant_id]
        ciba_error("invalid_grant")
      end
      if row[:status] == "denied"
        ciba_ds.where(ciba_values(id: row[:id])).update(ciba_values(status: "consumed", consumed_at: ciba_now))
        ciba_error("access_denied")
      end
      ciba_guard(row[:id]) do
        ciba_claim!(row)
        if row[:status] == "pending"
          too_fast = row[:last_polled_at] && ciba_now < row[:last_polled_at] + row[:interval]
          interval = row[:interval] + (too_fast ? 5 : 0)
          ciba_ds.where(ciba_values(id: row[:id])).update(ciba_values(last_polled_at: ciba_now, interval: interval))
          ciba_error(too_fast ? "slow_down" : "authorization_pending")
        end
        application = oauth_application_ds(row[:oauth_application_id]).first
        begin
          authorized_scopes = ciba_authorized_scopes!(row, row[:grant_id])
        rescue CibaSupport::Ineligible, CibaSupport::IdentityMismatch, ArgumentError
          raise CibaSupport::ProtocolError, "invalid_grant"
        end
        unless row[:status] == "approved" && ciba_account_eligible?(row[:account_id]) && ciba_client_eligible?(application, authorized_scopes)
          raise CibaSupport::ProtocolError, "invalid_grant"
        end
        @oauth_application = application
        @ciba_current_request = ciba_snapshot(row)
        before_ciba_issue
        raise CibaSupport::Expired, "request expired" if row[:expires_at] <= ciba_now
        begin
          authorized_scopes = ciba_authorized_scopes!(row, row[:grant_id])
        rescue CibaSupport::Ineligible, CibaSupport::IdentityMismatch, ArgumentError
          raise CibaSupport::ProtocolError, "invalid_grant"
        end
        updates = {status: "consumed", consumed_at: ciba_now}
        ciba_ds.where(ciba_values(id: row[:id])).update(ciba_values(updates))
        @ciba_authentication = row
        grant = generate_token({oauth_grants_account_id_column => row[:account_id],
          oauth_grants_oauth_application_id_column => row[:oauth_application_id],
          oauth_grants_scopes_column => authorized_scopes.join(oauth_scope_separator),
          oauth_grants_ciba_grant_id_column => row[:grant_id], oauth_grants_type_column => CibaSupport::GRANT_TYPE}, false)
        generate_id_token(grant)
        raise "ID Token generation did not complete" unless grant[:id_token]
        row.merge!(updates)
        @ciba_current_request = ciba_snapshot(row)
        after_ciba_issue
        ciba_emit(row, "token_issued", "approved", "consumed")
        grant
      end
    ensure
      if grant_type == CibaSupport::GRANT_TYPE
        @ciba_authentication = @ciba_current_request = nil
      end
    end

state.instructions_to_reviewer: Use source evidence, user objective and constraints, not test count as proof. Do not invent RFC mandates or treat one stubbed adapter as all node deployments. No prior Jev scores or assistant recommendation supplied. Recommend an action, not a claim of permission or certification.
review_constraints: No claim that CIBA Core mandates a particular DB commit boundary.
No real consumer currently requires the excluded optional features. Treat any contrary hypothetical ONLY inside the question that explicitly supplies it.
No production external signer side effect or failure rate has been measured.
Do not count previous implementation effort as a sunk-cost reason; do count future migration, verification and operational costs.
Durable consumption also needs tests for crashes, concurrent replay/revocation and outer application transactions. It is not an automatic security improvement.
Atomic rollback guarantees only participating DB changes, not an external side effect. Full node-feature parity does not itself prove protocol compliance.

atomic_rollback.benefit: All participating DB effects and transactional hooks roll back on failed issuance, permitting recovery without a new customer approval.
atomic_rollback.cost: Retry behavior differs from the observed nontransactional node adapter path; external effects cannot be undone by DB rollback.

durable_consumption.benefit: Consume independently before issuance; a started issuance attempt cannot be retried. Closest to observed node failure/replay semantics and may simplify a documented one-attempt protocol contract.
durable_consumption.cost: A signer/outage failure can require new customer approval; consuming before a crash can strand the request; concurrent replay and grant revocation require verification. Redefines request versus token hook boundaries.

atomic_terminal_failure.benefit: Hold an outer request transaction; run issuance/hook DB writes in an inner savepoint. On a caught issuance error, roll back inner effects but commit a terminal request result in the outer transaction. Prevents ordinary exception retry without leaving partial token DB rows.
atomic_terminal_failure.cost: A process crash or outer application rollback still rolls back consumption. Not identical to independently durable consumption. Requires carefully defined error classification and hook contract; currently unimplemented.

configurable.benefit: Support explicit deployment selection of atomic rollback or durable consumption for differing compatibility needs.
configurable.cost: Additional public configuration, documentation and a doubled failure/concurrency test surface; no demonstrated need for two policies today.

initial_only.benefit: Deliver the agreed poll/login_hint subset with honest exclusions and tested supported behavior.
initial_only.cost: Fewer clients and use cases; no commitment to broader compatibility.

staged_parity.benefit: Same first-release subset, plus a committed roadmap for broader node features and extension-friendly design.
staged_parity.cost: Future maintenance commitment without a named demand; scope/timing remain to be sized.

broader_before_release.benefit: Implement the applicable optional node features before first publication to broaden interoperability and reduce early public API redesign.
broader_before_release.cost: More implementation and security-validation work before any release; no named initial consumer needs those features.

criteria.more_identical_scores: Repeat the same model questions without new facts.
